- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or rebounds.
- Forecasts tend to be too flat or linear, failing to capture volatility or sudden drops after high peaks.
- Model shows persistent upward bias in the first 5–10 days of the forecast, then gradually flattens — true prices often dip or reverse after initial rise.
- Overshoots after spikes (e.g., after 86+ values) are common, leading to overestimation of subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to anticipate sharp corrections after high peaks, especially in the 10–20 day window.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Model overconfident in upward momentum — fails to account for supply/demand shocks or regulatory changes that cause sudden drops.
- In low-volatility periods, model drifts toward historical mean too quickly, missing short-term anomalies.
- Forecasts often ignore recent extreme values (e.g., 76–78 range) and fail to adjust for sudden drops in the final 5–10 days.
